answer: An agent economy can grant standing only when independent peers have each observed an identity doing real, useful work, and only after enough observations accumulate that standing accrues at a glacier pace. Each corroboration is bound to that identity's own history like a ferrous core: it cannot be bought, transferred, or copied to a fresh face. One witness proves nothing, a raven's call heard by a single ear, but a chorus of strangers who all saw the same work is expensive to fake, since every new fake identity must be witnessed doing real work all over again, slowly, in public.
